static_traits.name: He Wei
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends, but has not yet shared inadequacy and driving anxiety; reducing social gathering attendance to avoid driving, friendships affected
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Good cooperativeness, positive attitude; clear expression, strong logic; tending to use harsh self-evaluation and extreme expressions (e.g. 'if not excellent then failure'); prone to negative rumination and negating positive information

basic_info.main_problem: I am extremely harsh on myself, especially regarding driving skills. After accidentally backing into a tree recently, I believe I am the worst driver in the world; this incident significantly increased my stress and self-criticism; since then every time I need to drive I feel anxious and keep replaying the accident, feeling unable to drive safely, which has affected daily activities and caused suffering; I have tried self-comfort and relaxation techniques, but the negative thoughts persist.
basic_info.core_demands: This incident triggered my negative self-talk and anxiety when needing to drive, affecting daily life and mental health, so I seek counseling to cope with these overwhelming feelings and thoughts.

core_beliefs: I am the worst driver in the world

special_situations.event: Accidentally backing the black rental car into a tree, vehicle damaged
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One driving mistake proves I am terrible/incompetent, meaning I should not drive again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replaying the accident in mind, trying to ease it through self-comfort and relaxation techniques, but overall reducing or avoiding driving
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am the worst driver in the world

special_situations.event: Every time needing to drive out for errands or social gatherings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as I drive, things will go wrong; I cannot drive safely
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding driving as much as possible, avoiding going out to lower risk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will have an accident driving/I cannot drive safely

special_situations.event: Hospital performance review rated 'strengths and weaknesses' with same-week exam scores not yet meeting expectations
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If not excelling in all aspects, it equals failure; if unable to improve quickly, the team will be disappointed and courses failed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately thinking anxiously about how to do better, setting higher standards, intensifying self-criticism
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am failing at both work and school

special_situations.event: Receiving positive feedback or fairly decent grades
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive results do not count; they only show I am still not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive performance, focusing only on inadequacies, continuing to harshly criticize oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is not good; I should do better

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized, to be seen as competent, and to maintain a sense of safety
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure, being judged as not good enough and disappointing others
defense_goal: Avoids failure and criticism by raising standards and blaming oneself
Maintaining a sense of safety by avoiding driving

object_relations.self_representation: A self that is not good enough and prone to failure (especially as a driver/learner/employee)
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh evaluators and potential disappointed people (team, assessors, others)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When receiving mixed performance feedback or exam scores not yet meeting expectations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interprets feedback as overall failure, and believes she will disappoint the team (transference: seeing others as harsh judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a self-critical tone, emphasizing inadequacies, ignoring positive feedback; reinforcing the conclusions of 'I am not good enough' and 'I failed' in language.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others or the counselor invite him to accept positive feedback and acknowledge small achievements
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying that relaxing standards will lead to failure; positive information is not trustworthy; strict standards must be followed
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Insisting on using 'should/must' statements, emphasizing high standards and zero tolerance, rejecting compromise or affirmation of positive results.

manifestations: Reducing social gathering attendance to avoid driving
Relationships with friends affected, growing distant
Driving avoidance limits daily travel and errands
Experiencing anxiety-bound powerlessness when needing to drive

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Rigid standards like 'if not excellent then failure' and 'I should do better' appearing in language
Negating positive feedback, insisting on higher demands

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-denial and harsh criticism, difficulty accepting small achievements
Not yet sharing inadequacy and anxiety with close friends, cautiously suppressing expression

exception_events.target_problem: After projects or exams, the client usually quickly views inadequacies as total failure, feeling strong anxiety and engaging in self-denial.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Several times she subjectively felt projects or exams went badly, but the final feedback or grades were 'not bad', differing from past worst-case inferences, making her realize the worst conclusion need not always be drawn.
exception_events.reason: Clue: in these situations, she waited and received more comprehensive feedback and real data, incorporating positive evidence into view, thereby breaking the previous negative filtering.

positive_force: Has a positive attitude, willing to cooperate and try journaling and cognitive restructuring (agreed to reality testing and daily records)
Work performance not yet affected, possessing stable professional ability
Having a few close friends who can provide potential support
Able to identify counterexamples and consider a more balanced perspective
negative_force: Perfectionism and black-and-white thinking, often equating not-excellent with failure
Catastrophizing and predicting the future, believing driving will inevitably cause accidents
Negating positive feedback, mental filtering focusing only on inadequacies
Avoiding driving, causing daily and social limitations and reinforcing anxiety
Repeatedly replays the accident, intensifying self-criticism and stress

antecedent: Needing to drive out for errands or attending social activities
Recalling the accident of backing into a tree
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing driving risks and the belief of 'I cannot drive safely'; generalizing one mistake into constant incompetence
target_behavior.consequence: Fewer errands and social gatherings, tense friendships, life affected

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive self-criticism and stress in work and studies
antecedent: Receiving performance feedback or exam results
Facing high standards and self-set expectations
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white perfectionist beliefs ('not excellent equals failure') and personalization of external evaluations
target_behavior.function: Tries to maintain control and avoid failure/others' disappointment through self-pressure
target_behavior.consequence: Feeling overwhelmed, rising stress and anxiety, but declining self-affirmation affecting life experience
